extracted.intended_audience: authors and writers seeking professional manuscript editing and sensitivity-reading services
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on choosing the appropriate editorial service (developmental, line, proofreading, sensitivity reading), preparing and sending manuscripts, booking timelines, and payment procedures when working with a commercial editing provider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a developmental edit
rubrics_metrics.description: When you think about your manuscript in its entirety, ask yourself: Do you have concerns about the core narrative or plot? If so, a developmental edit might be your best route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use developmental editing when you need big-picture feedback on story structure, character arcs, pacing, and overall narrative problems. This is for manuscript-wide, structural concerns rather than sentence-level polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a line edit
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you more anxious about the rhythm, continuity, and flow? Then a line edit is what you're after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a line edit for sentence-level and paragraph-level improvements: rhythm, clarity, continuity, voice consistency, and smoothing prose rather than restructuring plot or scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a proofread
rubrics_metrics.description: For those meticulous details like grammar, spelling, and punctuation, a proofread is the way to go.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proofreading for final pass corrections of mechanics and typographical errors after substantive and line edits have been completed; not intended for developmental or large stylistic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a sensitivity read
rubrics_metrics.description: If you're aiming to ensure your content is inclusive and respectful, a sensitivity read is the ideal choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitivity reading focuses on representation and identifying potentially problematic portrayals, slurs, stereotypes, or misrepresentations of lived experience; useful when portraying marginalized identities or sensitive topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard manuscript format–Times New Roman, size 12, double spaced, one inch margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer Word documents but also work with Google Docs. If you send it in a different format, the editor will likely adjust it for ease of editing. Follow standard manuscript formatting to streamline the edit and reduce prep time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred file formats and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: We prefer Word documents, but also work with Google docs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit a different format, the team will likely convert or adjust it for ease of editing. Send in an editable format when possible to facilitate comments and tracked changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Booking lead time
rubrics_metrics.description: How far in advance should I book? This depends a great deal on the editor and services you want. We do have several editors who are consistently booked 6+ months out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and book according to the specific editor's availability; expect long lead times for in-demand editors and schedule accordingly to meet deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment method and invoice delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: We send invoices via Stripe. Sometimes they get flagged as spam, though, so check there if you haven't received it after we emailed. We can also send invoices via PayPal, but please ask for this specifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam folders for Stripe invoices; request PayPal explicitly if preferred. Be aware of the invoicing channel to avoid missed payments or delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment schedule (split payment policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: We split payments in half–you'll pay the first half on your start date and the final payment upon the completion of your edit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a 50/50 payment arrangement: initial deposit at start and remainder on delivery/completion. Plan your cashflow accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contact Salt & Sage
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill out our consult request form or email us at hello@saltandsagebooks.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the consult request form for a structured intake or email directly for inquiries. Contact is the primary route for booking, questions, and requesting alternative invoicing (e.g., PayPal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying an invoice online
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay my invoice — Click the button below to be taken to our Stripe payment portal to pay your invoice:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided 'Pay invoice' button to access the Stripe portal for online payment. If you haven't received an invoice link, check email (including spam) or contact support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsletter sign-up for updates and freebies
rubrics_metrics.description: Want freebies and updates? Sign up for our newsletter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscribe to receive occasional resources, updates about services, and promotional/free materials; useful for staying informed about offerings and learning resources.
